I be old man now, fifty-nine years, farming this small piece of land near my compound here for beans. The land na my own, so I no dey pay rent, and I go plant beans with small millet or sorghum between them like I always do — the beans help the soil. I no get plenty money for chemical fertilizer, but small urea I fit buy for the cereal wey dey intercrop, and I go carry manure from my goats and chickens to spread on am. My sons and wife go help me weed, and if the weeds too much when rain come heavy, I go call two or three young men from the village to help me for one or two days.
